summary: Describes a transparent cell transport service using the N-to-one cell relay mode for ATM pseudowires. It carries ATM cells over a packet network without interpreting them.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC describes carrying ATM cells between two ports over a packet-switched network. The customer equipment sees an ATM connection, while the provider-edge devices carry the cells through a pseudowire.

questions: what is atm transparent cell transport
how are atm cells carried over a packet network
how are atm cells mapped to a pseudowire
subtitle: A transparent service for carrying ATM cells over a packet-switched network.

tldr.problem: An operator may want to move ATM services onto a packet network without changing customer-edge ATM equipment.
tldr.mechanism: The ingress provider edge drops idle or unassigned cells and maps other cells to one pseudowire; the egress sends them without changing selected cell fields.
tldr.outcome: The service emulates a connection between ATM ports, while its security depends on the packet-switched network underneath.

today: RFC 4816 is a Proposed Standard. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: The Transparent Service
sections.content:
The service lets an operator migrate ATM services to a packet-switched network without provisioning the ATM subscriber or customer-edge devices. The RFC says those devices see the service as if connected by a Time Division Multiplexer leased line.

It is described as useful for connecting existing ATM switches over a faster packet network or providing ATM backhaul.
sections.plainLanguage: The service carries an ATM connection across a packet network without requiring changes to the customer ATM devices.

sections.title: Cell Relay Between ATM Ports
sections.content:
The service uses the N-to-one Virtual Circuit Connection cell-transport mode and MUST use pseudowire type 0x0003. The ingress provider edge drops idle or unassigned cells and maps all other cells from the port to a single pseudowire.

The egress provider edge does not change the VPI, VCI, PTI, or CLP bits. OAM cells and ILMI signalling from customer devices MUST be transported transparently.
sections.plainLanguage: The sending edge drops idle cells and places the others on one pseudowire. The receiving edge passes the cells along without changing the listed fields.

sections.title: Concatenation, Failures, and Security
sections.content:
Cell concatenation MAY save packet-network bandwidth, but both provider edges must agree. When the pseudowire setup provides a maximum concatenation value, the ingress edge must not exceed it and must not concatenate if the egress edge omitted it.

If the packet network or pseudowire fails, the edges do not generate OAM cells; they bring down the ATM interfaces. The RFC says service security is only as strong as the packet network and congestion considerations follow RFC 4717.
sections.plainLanguage: The edges may combine cells only when they agree on the limit. If the underlying path fails, they indicate a failure on the ATM interfaces.

references.text: Martini, L., et al., "Encapsulation Methods for Transport of Asynchronous Transfer Mode (ATM) over MPLS Networks", RFC 4717, December 2006.
